title.narrative: Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to strengthen policies and programs to ensure equal opportunities and treatment for men, women, PwDs and other groups in vulnerable situations

description.narrative: Decent work is the ILO’s primary goal for Indonesia, including for women, minority group, and people in vulnerable situations. The office has continuously working to equal employment opportunities, reducing stigma and discriminations these target groups. The ILO is addressing challenges faced, for example, by people with disabilities, and women workers, minorities such as refugees, people living with HIV, and other disadvantage groups in accessing decent work and livelihood opportunities. ILO focused to promote decent work in care economy, including to support Government in developing policy related to care work. Some of the work that the office currently (and will be continuously) doing is: (1) advocating and fostering the gender equality, human rights approach for people with disabilities and social security and promoting social investments in care services for childcare in particular in order to address the double burden of work and family responsibilities, in particular for women, through research, knowledge sharing, technical advises, and capacity building; (2) technical and soft skill training, leveraging peer learning and support network to facilitate development, growth and enhancement of women and minority groups enterprises; (3) empowering community by entrepreneurships and social enterprise; (4) promoting international labour standards and its implementation/ awareness raising activities in the country; (5) facilitating linkages between private sector firms, social partner institutions and training centers to ensure greater opportunity through higher entry, retention and advancement of women worker, people with disabilities and other community in vulnerable situations. The intended outcomes will contribute to outcome 1 of the UNSDCF – People living in Indonesia, especially those at risk of being left furthest behind, are empowered to fulfil human development potentials as members of inclusive and just society.
